headline: Confusion reigns among NYC homeowners over eligibility for Mamdani's new pied-à-terre tax
summary: Nearly a week after city tax officials released information on who could be on the hook for the new pied-à-terre tax on second homes worth over $5 million, attorneys and homeowners say they are baffled by the process overseen by Mayor Mamdani's administration. A City Hall official clarified that letters were sent to roughly 17,000 addresses suspected of being second homes.

headline: Rocket Lab stock jumps on new multi-launch Electron agreement with Japan's iQPS
summary: Rocket Lab shares jumped over 8% after the company disclosed a new multi-launch agreement with Japanese satellite firm iQPS (Institute for Q-shu Pioneers of Space), securing three additional dedicated Electron launches, even as the stock remains well off its late-May peak.

headline: Delcy Rodríguez opens Venezuela's oil sector to foreign investors as ExxonMobil, Halliburton return
summary: Venezuela's acting president Delcy Rodríguez is courting long-term investment in the country's resource-rich oil sector at international summits, as a new law ends PDVSA's monopoly and gives private companies control over production, sales and independent arbitration of disputes. American companies including ExxonMobil, ConocoPhillips, Halliburton and GE Vernova are returning or negotiating new investments as signs of economic recovery emerge in Caracas.

headline: Trump's net approval rating hits new second-term low of -20.6 heading into midterms
summary: Trump's net approval rating hit a new second-term low of -20.6 as of July 31, with disapproval nearing 60% and only 21% of Americans saying they strongly approve of his performance. His net approval among men in an Economist/YouGov poll was -22, the lowest ever recorded in either of his terms, with cost-of-living and the Iran conflict cited as drags.

headline: Ukraine strikes Engels-2 strategic bomber base and Saratov oil refinery in major deep-strike raid
summary: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed drone strikes overnight Aug 1-2 on Rosneft's Saratov oil refinery (hitting its main crude distillation unit) and the nearby Engels-2 strategic aviation airbase, which hosts Tu-160, Tu-95MS and Tu-22M3 bombers. Ukrainian forces also hit a fuel depot in Kaluga Oblast and a drone storage/launch site near Navlya in Bryansk Oblast. President Zelensky confirmed the strikes.

headline: Mamdani and Finance Commissioner extend pied-a-terre tax exemption deadline after confusing rollout
summary: Following confusion after the Department of Finance posted a database of 900,000+ properties that "may" be subject to the new non-primary-residence surcharge (city says only ~17,000 addresses worth over $5M actually got notice letters), Mayor Mamdani and Commissioner Richard Lee announced a four-week extension, giving homeowners until Sept. 18, 2026 (from Aug. 21) to file exemption appeals.

headline: Trump calls off planned new strikes on Iran, citing progress on Hormuz-reopening deal
summary: Trump announced he is holding off a pending attack on Iran after Qatar-mediated talks with Iran, Oman and the US produced the outlines of a deal: immediate, complete reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and an end to Iran nuclear weapons development. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman had called Trump urging him not to strike. Iranian state media has not confirmed the framework and shows no sign Tehran has shifted its stance on Hormuz.

headline: Senate stopgap funding bill release slips as negotiations drag ahead of August recess
summary: Senate appropriators had hoped to unveil text for a stopgap measure funding the government into early December before the weekend, but release is slipping to early next week amid disputes over a Trump administration grant-rule provision giving political appointees more sway over federal grant approvals. The House already passed its own stopgap through Dec. 4; the Senate is preparing an alternative before a procedural vote on the funding vehicle needed to avert an Oct. 1 shutdown.

headline: Foreign investors gather in London to plan re-entry into Venezuelan oil sector
summary: About 200 energy-industry figures met at a London hotel to discuss investing in Venezuelan oil, a prospect unthinkable eight months ago. Apertura Energy CEO Greig Gilbert declared "the time is now"; Kpler analyst Homayoun Falakshahi estimated Venezuela needs $50-100 billion in investment over 5-10 years. Speakers cited decaying infrastructure, political uncertainty and earthquake damage as roadblocks. The event previews the bigger Venezuela Energy Week conference set for October in Caracas.

headline: SpaceX posts first earnings as a public company; Starlink tops 12M subscribers ahead of $120B insider lockup unlock
summary: SpaceX released its first quarterly (Q2 2026) earnings report as a public company after markets closed Aug. 4, with shares up about 6% at the open despite trading more than 50% below its post-IPO high. Starlink subscriber count surpassed 12 million and was the company's only profitable business last year, generating $4.42 billion in income. The earnings date also triggers the first tranche of a staggered insider share unlock beginning Aug. 6, potentially freeing up to 911.5 million shares (roughly $120B) held by early investors and employees; Elon Musk's own ~6.4 billion-share stake remains under a separate 366-day lockup.

headline: Mamdani dismisses entire business advisory board of NYC's Mayor's Fund
summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani dismissed the business and civic leaders who advised the Mayor's Fund to Advance New York City, the multimillion-dollar philanthropic arm that channels private donations into public programs. The city said the entire board of advisers was disbanded, thanking members for their service; it marks the first time in at least three mayoral administrations that all members of the advisory group were dismissed at once.
